properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 26 at 12:01PM CDT until October 26 at 3:00PM CDT by NWS Amarillo TX
properties.description:

rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...South Central Hutchinson County in the panhandle of
Texas...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Ponding of water in urban or other areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.3 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Borger.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 10:13AM MDT until October 30 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Puerco Near Bernardo affecting Socorro County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Puerco near Bernardo.

* WHEN...Until late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, Streets in the village of San Francisco
between interstate 25 and the Rio Grande just south of Bernardo are
being flooded. Water levels in the Lower Rio Puerco have not been
this high since July of 1944. The nearby railroad bridge may also
be flooded. Further rises will impact Interstate 25 traffic.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:00 PM MDT Sunday the stage was 20.0 feet. No reliable
observations available thereafter.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will is forecast to remain at flood stage,
reaching around 22.8 feet this afternoon. It will then fall early
tomorrow afternoon, then it will rise to 22.5 feet Wednesday
morning. It will then fall below flood stage early Thursday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 19.5 feet.
- Flood History...No available flood history.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 9:50AM CDT until October 27 at 4:00AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Presidio Vehicle Bridge affecting
Presidio County.

For the Rio Grande...including Rio Grande at Presidio Vehicle
Bridge...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Presidio Vehicle Bridge.

* WHEN...From this morning to late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, the river reaches bankfull, after which the
flood plain between the levees begins to flood.  No damage is
expected. At 15.5 feet, the river reaches minor flood stage, and
flooding between the levees occurs.  No damage to structures is
expected. At 20.0 feet, the river reaches moderate flood stage,
inundating the plain between the levees.  Erosion of the levees is
likely.  Water may seep through the levees, flooding adjacent
farmland. At 22.9 feet, the river reaches major flood stage.  While
water remains between the levees at Presidio, areas downstream may
experience significant flooding.  FM 170 downstream of Presidio
will flood in low spots.  Farmland along the river will be
inundated. At 25.0 feet, the river remains between the levees at
Presidio, although continued flows at this level could cause damage
to the levees.  FM 170 downstream will likely be flooded and
impassable in spots.  Farmland around the river will continue to
inundate. At 25.8 feet, the river reaches record stage for the
period of record (1978).  A higher stage was reached in 1932, but
the exact stage is unknown.  FM 170 will be flooded downstream of
Presidio.  Farmland around the river will remain inundated. At 28.2
feet, the river reaches record stage for the period of record
(1978).  A higher stage was reached in 1932, but the exact stage is
unknown.  FM 170 remains flooded downstream of Presidio.  Farmland
adjacent to the river remains inundated. At 30.0 feet, The top of
the levee is reached, and water will begin to overtop the levees.
Major flooding of Presidio and surrounding farmland is likely.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM CDT Monday the stage was 40.6 feet (12.4 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet (3.7 meters).
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM CDT Monday was 40.6 feet (12.4 meters).
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this afternoon and continue falling to 4.2 feet (1.3 meters)
Saturday morning.
- Flood stage is 15.5 feet (4.7 meters).
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet (8.6 meters) on 09/16/2008.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1000 PM CDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 9:55AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent gusty northeast winds are causing river levels to rise on
the St Johns at Astor, currently in Moderate Flood Stage. The river
is forecast to continue to climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage
early this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EDT Monday the stage was 3.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EDT Monday was 3.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.8 feet
this evening.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
